bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Selloff: Worst Week for Semis/AI Names Since 2023
bullets.body: SOX fell 11.4% and the MS AI Tech Beneficiaries basket dropped 16.5% w/w — worst week since launch — as investors repriced AI capex economics, debt sustainability, and ROI visibility. CoreWeave CDS hit a record ~1,194bp (>60% default probability implied), AI lab revenue concerns mounted after Anthropic's Q3 ARR tracked toward $75B vs. $100B+ investor expectations, and equal-weight S&P outpaced cap-weighted by 225bp. GS Prime reports hedge funds reversed all 2025 net AI-stock buying in six consecutive sessions, with US Info Tech the most net-sold global sector on record.

bullets.title: CRWV: Debt Concerns 'Overdone' per JPM; Upgraded to Overweight Despite Record CDS
bullets.body: JPM raised CRWV to Overweight, arguing the sell-off is driven by sentiment around cash-flow timing, not contract economics. Capacity is pre-sold under long-term take-or-pay contracts with mid-teens unlevered IRR vs. 9–11% cost of capital; FCF inflection expected by 2030E as active-to-annual-capacity ratio reaches ~4.5x. NVDA CEO Jensen Huang publicly defended CoreWeave's financial strength and improving cost of capital, sparking a +6% close on Oct 15.

bullets.title: NFLX: CCO Replaced; ~8.9% Implied Move; Q3 In-Line vs. Guide
bullets.body: Netflix replaced longtime Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria with ex-Disney/Fox exec Peter Rice effective Oct 26, rattling shares 3.3–3.7% pre-market. Q3 consensus sits at $12.87B revenue/$0.82 EPS — in line with company guidance — with bulls citing pricing power, ad monetization, and NBCU synergies; bears flag slowing engagement (global Top-10 viewing hours -11% in Q3), rising churn, and CCO transition risk. Options imply ~8.9% move; Jefferies maintains Buy at $85 PT on 22% 3-yr EPS CAGR.

bullets.title: META: Muse Wonder Launch Drives +4%; JPM Upgrades to OW; PT Range $800–$920
bullets.body: Meta launched Muse Wonder and Wonder Full frontier-class AI models, reclaiming the #1 iOS App Store spot and driving the stock +3–4%. JPM upgraded META to Overweight citing AMZN/GOOGL-style AI monetization optionality; PT $920 on 26x '28E EPS of $35.45. Citi raised PT to $895/$800, while UBS lifted to $884. Key 3Q debate: $10B legal expense accrual and 2027 Opex/Capex guidance ($210–250B range). Q3 earnings on Oct 21 after close; consensus $6.59–6.76 EPS, $63.3B revenue.

bullets.title: TSLA: Morgan Stanley More Constructive; Roadster Unveil; Robotaxi Scaling
bullets.body: MS analyst turned more constructive on Tesla after the Cybercab fleet scaled to 300+ vehicles in 30 days with 1M+ unsupervised miles in Austin. Tesla unveiled the new Roadster with SpaceX thrusters at an event, lifting shares +3–5% pre-market. 3Q earnings due week of Oct 20; Hedgeye's Risk Range model changed TSLA from Bullish to Neutral on Oct 15.

bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen Defends AI Ecosystem; ~80% Infra Revenue Share; GTC Berlin Oct 20–22
bullets.body: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang called for renewed US-China AI dialogue, defended CoreWeave publicly, and stated Rubin GPU shipments are in full production (though tracking ~5–7K VR NVL72 racks vs. 75–80K total). MS AI capex estimates raised 14% to $1.6T (+60% y/y) in 2027, with NVDA controlling ~80% of AI infrastructure revenue share. NVDA GTC Berlin (Oct 20–22) is the next major catalyst. Germany-NVDA AI partnership talks reportedly involve several hundred million euros.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone Duo Preorders Launch; +2% Pre-Market; Delivery into Late January
bullets.body: iPhone Duo preorders launched at 8am ET Oct 16, with delivery timelines immediately extending to late January — widely interpreted as a strong demand signal. Apple closed above $5T market cap; shares +2% pre-market. Separately, Apple unveiled HomeView ($299 smart display) and is partnering with Meta to bring open-weight Muse models to Mac. iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max orders reportedly cut ~15% (a bearish signal from earlier in the week), and iPhone Q3 shipments beat at 57.3M units (+22% share).

bullets.title: ACN: UBS Upgrades to Buy ($278 PT); FY27–29 Outlook Beats Street
bullets.body: UBS upgraded Accenture to Buy with a $278 PT following the Investor Day, which introduced the company's first multi-year guidance: mid-single-digit CC revenue growth in FY27–28 accelerating to mid-to-high single digits in FY29. Emerging Alliances bookings tripled YoY; AI & data workforce grew to 110K; fixed-price contracts now >65% of bookings. JPM and Mizuho also constructive; stock rallied ~25% post-Oct 1 earnings. ACN acquired UK data firm Sagacity Solutions and launched a Workday FDE agentic AI program.

bullets.title: MU: IR Call Confirms 75%+ FY27 Supply Committed; $33B Buyback; HBM Prices Rising
bullets.body: UBS hosted an MU IR call post-strong F4Q26/F1Q27 guidance. Key takeaways: 75%+ of FY27 supply committed via SCAs (35%+ of revenue through 2030); HBM bit shipments grow faster than DRAM through 2028 with significant pricing increases; data center alone $10B in F4Q26; $33B new buyback authorization (3x prior). CXMT's 4F² DRAM claims created near-term pressure (MU -4–5% in the week) but analysts view commercial risk as limited near-term.

bullets.title: TSM: Raised FY26 Revenue Guide to +44%; N2 Capacity to Double in 2027
bullets.body: TSMC posted Q3 revenue of $46.7B (beat vs. $45.4B consensus) and raised FY26 growth to +44% y/y (from +40%) on sustained AI/HPC demand. Q4 guided to $53.3B vs. $50.1B consensus. N2 accounted for ~8% of wafer revenue and will more than double in capacity by 2027. AI accelerator CAGR guidance revised above prior 'mid-high 50s%.' JPM upgraded TSM to Overweight, targeting NT$3,300 on accelerating capacity ramp into 2028; UBS raising 2027–28 capex estimates.

bullets.title: TXN: Top Analog Semis Pick at UBS/JPM; Q3 Earnings Oct 21
bullets.body: TXN remains top pick in analog semis per UBS, with positive research thesis intact into Q3 earnings (Oct 21, consensus $2.42 EPS / $5.92B revenue). Pricing improving, auto segment 'less bad,' and data center exposure growing. Buyside consensus expects flat Q4 guide vs. Street's -3% estimate, suggesting upside surprise potential.

bullets.title: SHOP: Price Increases 13–20%; Pricing Power Signal; Not Material to 2027
bullets.body: Shopify raised Grow/Advanced tier annual plan pricing ~13–20% (US new customers only) and Basic tier pricing ex-US. UBS estimates immaterial FY2027 impact but views the move as confirmatory of pricing power, consistent with CFO commentary on higher frequency pricing. UBS maintains Neutral. JPM expert call with Shopify Platinum Partner Zettler Digital (Oct 19) to discuss AI-commerce strategy and SMB demand trends.

bullets.title: T: Selling Mexico Wireless for $2B; Bernstein Downgrades; Starlink Risk Debate
bullets.body: AT&T agreed to sell AT&T Mexico to Grupo Televisa/Fintech Holdings for $2B cash (closing Q1 2027) to focus on US fiber/wireless. Bernstein downgraded T to Market Perform (PT $24) citing prolonged Starlink competitive pressure and Q4 seasonality. MS reiterates Overweight on T, noting SpaceX more likely to be a network-based competitor, and the selloff (T -10–11% on Oct 9 SpaceX spectrum news) is overdone. EchoStar (ECHO) upgraded to Overweight at JPM with $144 PT on 40–50% NAV discount.

bullets.title: FOXA: Upgraded to Buy at BofA (+$54 PT to $85); Roku Acquisition Approved
bullets.body: BofA upgraded Fox Corporation to Buy from Underperform, raising PT to $85 (+57%, implying 33% upside), following Roku shareholder approval of Fox's $160/share acquisition. DOJ Second Request extends review, with deal expected to close H1 2027. FOXA +3.5–3.7% pre-market on Oct 16.

bullets.title: EXPE/BKNG/ABNB: Agentic AI Threatens OTA Commission Pools
bullets.body: Hedgeye upgraded ABNB to Best Idea Long ($190–220 target) on hotel push strategy and limited AI disruption risk; put EXPE in Short Bias on weak comps, poor product mix, and high exposure to agentic disruption; rated BKNG Neutral. OTA stocks down 15–25% following Meta Muse/Instinct launches that complete full travel bookings via browser automation, bypassing OTA intermediaries entirely. BKNG launched 'Vayo' AI travel agent with $100M investment.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure 46–47% CC Beat Expected; CIO Survey Leader; Maia 300 Announced
bullets.body: Citi and Mizuho raised MSFT PT to $636/$600 respectively ahead of Q3 earnings (Oct 28). CIO surveys show MSFT as the #1 AI vendor gaining incremental spend share. Microsoft unveiled Maia 300 (40% better tokens/megawatt vs. leading GPUs) for 2027 deployment, reducing NVDA reliance. UK CMA proposed Strategic Market Status designation in business software. Azure group head reportedly asked for 20%+ cost cuts; MSFT disputes accuracy.

bullets.title: GOOGL: GCP +91–105% YoY; Gemini 4 Argon Launches; JPM Top Internet Pick
bullets.body: JPM upgraded Google Cloud growth estimates to +100% in Q3 and +105% in Q4 on TPU revenue ramp, and raised the 2027 GCP forecast to $219B (+105% y/y). PT raised to $425. Gemini 4 Argon launched globally, matching GPT-6 Astra on the Intelligence Index at 60% of cost per task. Analysts note the 'self-improvement critical moment' in Google's Argon AI model. GOOGL rolling out hotel booking in AI Mode (negative for OTAs). Q3 earnings Oct 27.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY OSB GGR -24% YoY in Wk Ending 10/11; Indiana/Missouri Solid; PM Spend Hitting EBITDA
bullets.body: NY online sports betting GGR declined 24% y/y (hold rate -345bp to 9%) for the week ending Oct 11, with DraftKings at -21% y/y though maintaining 32% share. Citi cut DKNG EBITDA estimates by $50–70M per quarter on prediction market customer acquisition spend, lowering PT to $28 (14x 2027 EBITDA). Indiana (+5% y/y) and Missouri (+5% y/y) gaming revenues were more constructive in September. NFL Week 5 results (60% public favorites winning) created additional hold headwinds.

bullets.title: WDC/SNDK: Memory Stocks Hammered; CXMT 4F² DRAM Claims; 8-Session SOX Losing Streak
bullets.body: WDC and SNDK fell 5–7% in the week, with the broader SOX index down eight consecutive sessions (tied for longest since 2006), off 15%+ from peak. CXMT announced a 4F² DDR5 RDIMM launch by year-end 2026 — approximately two years ahead of Samsung — triggering a global memory selloff. Analysts are skeptical on mass-production viability but acknowledge real capex investment from CXMT. WDC reports Q3 earnings Oct 22 (consensus $4.08 EPS / $4.14B revenue).

bullets.title: SMTC/SMCI: SMTC Data Center CAGR 75% Through FY30; SMCI Raised Q3 Guide
bullets.body: Oppenheimer and Roth upgraded Semtech (SMTC) to Buy/Outperform with $220–225 PTs after an Analyst Day showed a 38% revenue CAGR through FY29 with data center growing at 75% CAGR to $2.1B; gross margins expanding 600bp to 70%. SMCI raised Q3 FY27 EPS guide to $1.14 (+/- $0.02) from $1.05 and guided FY27–FY28 revenue growth >2x each year; Northland upgraded to Outperform at $186 PT. SMCI CFO appointment (Mark Long from WDC) removes governance overhang but financing scrutiny remains.
